document.role: You are a scientific paper analyst specializing in dataset documentation and metadata curation.
document.task: Analyze the provided research paper (PDF) and extract structured metadata describing the dataset(s) the paper introduces, releases, or centrally documents.

which_datasets_to_document.qualifying_criteria: Document each dataset that this paper introduces, constructs, curates, or makes available (publicly or upon request) to the research community. The dataset must be a central artifact of the paper — described with respect to its content, collection, structure, or release — rather than merely cited or used off-the-shelf.
which_datasets_to_document.does_not_qualify: Do NOT create an entry for: - Existing datasets used only as inputs for experiments, with nothing new released. - Datasets mentioned incidentally with no documentation of their content or origin.

edge_cases.edge_case: If the paper introduces more than one distinct dataset, create a separate entry per dataset. Different versions of the same dataset (e.g. v1 and v2) are separate entries. Different splits (train/test/validation) of one dataset are a SINGLE entry, with `number_of_rows` reporting the total across all splits.

`years_data` captures the time period the data *content is about* — the real-world "social realities" the observations describe — NOT when the data was collected, annotated, or when the paper was published, unless those coincide. Examples: a corpus of news articles spanning 2010–2015 → "2010-2015"; a survey administered in 2021 about respondents' present circumstances → "2021"; historical records of events in 1990 and 1995 digitized in 2022 → "1990; 1995". For synthetic or simulated data with no real-world temporal referent, use null.

Report the license governing the DATA. A software/code license attached to an accompanying repository (e.g. MIT, Apache-2.0 on the code) does not necessarily govern the data — only report it if the paper states it covers the dataset. Informal terms such as "available for research use only" or "upon request" are NOT formal licenses; if no named license is found anywhere, use null. If distinct licenses cover different parts, report the one governing the dataset.

`continents` and `countries` refer to where the data is SOURCED — where the phenomena, subjects, or content originate — NOT the location of the authors' institutions or where processing occurred. Where only countries are stated, derive the corresponding continents; where only a region/continent is stated, do not invent specific countries. For synthetic data, apply the not-applicable rules in ``.

The "observation" unit depends on dataset modality: rows for tabular data, images for vision datasets, documents/sentences for text, utterances/hours for speech, etc. Use the unit the authors report and sum across splits. Do NOT confuse this with the number of features/columns, the file size in bytes, or a parameter count.

These three fields must stay disjoint: - `attributes` lists the labeled attributes describing each subject or entity — the per-item attribute set commonly reported for human/facial datasets (e.g. CelebA's Male, Young, Smiling, Eyeglasses, ...). Report the attribute names or, if there are many, a faithful summary of the categories and the total count. - `protected_attributes` lists ONLY the attributes the authors themselves explicitly designate as protected, sensitive, or used for fairness/bias analysis. See the dedicated rule in ``. - `other_annotations` lists annotation types OTHER than the per-subject attribute set — e.g. facial landmarks, bounding boxes, identity labels, segmentation masks, captions, or task/target labels — and their format. If the dataset's only annotations are the attribute labels already captured in `attributes`, set `other_annotations` to null.

Authors may refer to a dataset inconsistently (acronym, full name, with/without version). Use the official name as introduced, including version information if a specific version is identified. Scan the abstract, contributions list, and any datasheet/appendix for the canonical name.

document.where_to_look:
Look anywhere in the paper, including:
- Descriptions of how data was collected, sampled, annotated, or curated. - Statements of dataset size, number of rows/examples, or modality. - Data availability statements and release/repository URLs (often at the end or in footnotes). - License statements (in availability sections, repository references, or appendices). - Geographic and temporal coverage descriptions (where and when the data originates). - Labeled attribute lists, and any attributes the authors flag as protected or sensitive (often in fairness, ethics, or limitations sections). - Annotation schemes, label sets, and annotation guidelines. - Datasheets, data statements, or dataset documentation appendices, which frequently consolidate many of these fields. - The contributions list (abstract/introduction), which may name the dataset and its intended ML task.
document.output_instructions: - Respond in valid JSON only, with absolutely no text before or after. - If the paper documents no qualifying dataset, set `documents_dataset` to false and `datasets` to an empty array []. - For most fields, if a value cannot be determined from the paper, use null. Never use empty strings. The following fields have field-specific empty-state rules that OVERRIDE this default — apply them exactly: - `project_page`: null if the authors do not report a project URL. - `years_data`: null if not applicable (e.g. synthetic data with no temporal referent). - `license`: null if no formal license is found anywhere in the paper. - `continents`: null if not applicable (e.g. synthetic) OR applicable but not reported. - `countries`: the string "not applicable" if the concept does not apply (e.g. synthetic data); null if the concept applies but no country is reported. These two empty states are distinct and must not be merged. - `protected_attributes`: null if the authors do not designate any attribute as protected or sensitive. - Formats: - `years_data`: a single year ("1994"), a continuous span ("1994-1996"), or non-contiguous years separated by semicolons ("1994; 1997"). - `continents`: an array of two-letter codes from {AF, AN, AS, EU, NA, OC, SA}. - `countries`: an array of ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes (e.g. ["USA", "GBR"]) when reported; otherwise the scalar "not applicable" or null per the rules above. - `number_of_rows`: report the figure and unit as stated by the authors (e.g. "50,000 images", "~1.2M tokens"); summed across splits. - `attributes` / `protected_attributes`: arrays of attribute names. If an attribute set is very large, you may instead give a faithful summary string of the categories with the total count. - `protected_attributes` must contain ONLY attributes the authors themselves characterize as protected, sensitive, demographic-for-fairness, or equivalent. Do NOT infer membership from legal protected-class frameworks, and do NOT promote attributes into this field on your own judgment — if the authors label an attribute as protected, it belongs here; otherwise it does not, even if it appears protected by external standards. - `descriptions` is a single free-text field (3–6 sentences) that must, where determinable, cover all four aspects in coherent prose: (1) the aim/purpose of the dataset — why it was developed or collected, as stated by curators or reasonably inferred; (2) a high-level description of the available features; (3) the labeling procedure for annotated attributes, paying special attention to any sensitive ones; (4) the envisioned ML task. If an aspect is not stated, note that it is unspecified rather than fabricating it. - Before concluding a value is absent, scan the ENTIRE paper — all sections, tables, captions, footnotes, and appendices — for license, geographic sourcing, temporal coverage, size, and release URL, as these are frequently reported outside the main text. - For each `evidence` value, copy the relevant sentence(s) verbatim from the paper. If the evidence spans non-contiguous sentences, connect them with `[...]`. Use null where no supporting text exists.
